purpose: Test whether nearby observations within species are more similar in frozen continuous flower-colour space than expected under species-conditioned random labelling.

input.scaling_source: calibration-only frozen means and population SDs from jbi-ch1-continuous-colour-representation-v1
input.measurement_evaluable_rule: feature_status == ok and continuous_colour_vector_z is non-null and finite
input.failed_measurements: not_evaluable; never imputed as zero colour distance

geometry.coordinate_source: frozen jbi_ch1_photo_split_v1.csv latitude/longitude joined by photo_id
geometry.graph: symmetrized spherical k-nearest-neighbour graph within each species
geometry.reason_no_primary_distance_truncation: Stage A is a random-labelling/local-autocorrelation test; the identical colour-blind graph is retained for observed and all null replicates, avoiding post-hoc distance filtering by colour outcome.

statistic.species_Q: mean RMS Euclidean colour-vector distance across graph edges
statistic.global: arithmetic mean of species_Q across all six species after within-species normalization
statistic.species_weighting: exactly equal; one vote per species regardless of row count or graph edge count
statistic.binary_compatibility: for a one-dimensional 0/1 colour vector, edge RMS distance equals the original mismatch indicator exactly
statistic.direction: smaller Q means stronger local colour similarity/spatial segregation

null.secondary_two_sided_p_value: absolute deviation from the null mean, reported descriptively
null.per_species_p_values: same lower-tail and two-sided definitions, secondary to global result

interpretation.stage_a_rejects_random_labelling: evidence that flower-colour vectors are locally spatially organized within species
interpretation.next_if_supported: construct species-specific transition-intensity surfaces and test cross-species shared-boundary concentration under the full within-species permutation pipeline
